random_seed_note: Live ARC-AGI-3 API replay of pre-computed action sequences; no RNG invoked by this driver.
duration_note: Sum of the three live sessions this run: the 25-game package re-validation (~8 min), the bp35/lf52 deep-win attempt (~7.5 min), and the instrumented lf52 diagnostic re-run (~5 min). All real network round-trips against https://three.arcprize.org.
narrative: Operator-directed follow-up to the earlier replay ledger: 'Fix the sc25 drift and re-validate all games.' PART 1 (the requested scope): ran scripts/arc3_live_submit.py (VALIDATE mode, no --submit, no scorecard close, no leaderboard record) against the real live ARC-AGI-3 API using the existing package (experiment_4679_submission_package_operator_resubmit.json, 25 games / 60 claimed levels). Result: 25/25 games env-matched, including sc25 (claimed L5 -> LIVE L5 MATCH). This confirms commit a09892c5a's WARMUP_GAMES fix (sc25's first env.step after reset is silently consumed as a no-op; the live driver now prepends the same throwaway warmup step arc3_replay_scorecard_metaharness.py's replay_game() already used) genuinely resolves the 2026-07-15 drift, which had never been re-tested live since the fix landed 18 minutes after that failed run. PART 2 (bonus, beyond the literal ask): the package used in Part 1 is stale (last refreshed 2026-06-24) and caps bp35/lf52 at L1, far below their true 2026-07-17 registry depth (bp35 9/9, lf52 10/10, both solved same-day, same session). Since fully-verified flat action sequences for both already existed (bp35: 410 actions, results/outer_loop_round26_bp35_probe_l9_20260717.json; lf52: 1009 actions, results/outer_loop_lf52_l8plus_probe_20260717.json), replayed them live directly on a fresh dedicated scorecard to test whether today's offline wins actually hold on the real environment. bp35: CLEAN MATCH -- claimed L9, LIVE L9, all 410 actions replayed without error (163s). lf52: FAILED at action 849 of 1009 -- a genuinely new, different problem from sc25's warmup bug. An instrumented re-run (fresh scorecard, per-action try/except) confirmed level progress is real and correct through L8 (0->1->2->3->4->5->6->7->8 at actions 7/41/145/213/311/614/758/826, matching the offline artifact's L8 boundary at action 827 almost exactly) but fails immediately at action 849, 22 actions into the L9 tail, with HTTP 400 Bad Request from https://three.arcprize.org/api/cmd/ACTION6. Root cause identified with full confidence: action 849 clicks pixel (132,18); the visible live frame is 64x64 (valid pixel range 0-63), so x=132 is out of bounds. Un-transforming lf52's own documented pixel<->source-grid formula (frame_xy = 6*grid_xy + 6, per this game's registry gotcha) gives source grid x=21 -- an exact match for the registry's own L9 gotcha text, which explicitly describes 'two off-screen blue pegs...legally leapfrogged from source x=20/21 back to x=11/12' as part of the winning route. A full scan of the 1009-action sequence found exactly 22 such out-of-bounds clicks, all contiguous (actions 849-870ish), all part of this same off-screen relay maneuver; none appear anywhere in the L1-L8 prefix (actions 0-826), which is exactly why L8 replayed cleanly live while L9 did not. CONCLUSION: the OFFLINE arc_agi arcade accepts and correctly routes ACTION6 clicks with pixel coordinates outside the visible 0-63 frame (addressing off-screen game objects directly by their source-grid position); the LIVE API validates coordinates strictly and rejects anything outside 0-63 with HTTP 400. This is a real, structural permissiveness gap between the offline dev environment and the live scored environment -- not a bug in this driver, not a warmup-step issue, and not something a quick patch can fix, since the winning L9 route as banked genuinely depends on a live-invalid interaction. Whether the SAME off-screen game-state manipulation is achievable live via some in-bounds equivalent (e.g. scrolling the camera into position first via legitimate moves, then clicking the same logical target in-frame) is unknown and would require genuine live exploration to determine -- deliberately NOT attempted in this session, since that is real new-mechanism-discovery work, not a re-validation task. No credit change: this does not retract lf52's OFFLINE registry credit (10/10, verified via 5x fresh offline-arcade replay + official reproduce() gate, per commit c588364d7 -- those claims stand, unaffected by live-API coordinate validation differences). It does mean lf52's L9-L10 win is not currently live-submittable as banked.

acceptance_gates.condition: sc25 fix must be confirmed via a real live network call, not just code inspection
acceptance_gates.principle: A code fix that was never re-tested live is a claim, not a verification.

acceptance_gates.condition: Any new finding (the lf52 out-of-bounds issue) must be root-caused with reproducible evidence, not just reported as an opaque failure
acceptance_gates.principle: An unexplained live failure is not actionable; the exact action index, coordinate, and un-transformed source meaning must be shown.

honest_verdict.principle: The verdict must reflect both the successful requested fix AND the new problem found, not overstate success by omitting the lf52 finding.
